8-S/4 of 2018, titled as, 'Manjeet Singh versus the Secretary & anr.'.

sentences.text:
Section 74 of the Act is reproduced as under:
"74. Appeal to High Court- (1) The Requiring Body or any person aggrieved by the Award passed by an Authority under section 69 may file an appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of Award:
Provided that the High Court may, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the said period, allow it to be filed within a further period not exceeding sixty days.

(2) Every appeal referred to under sub-section (1) shall be heard as expeditiously as possible and endeavour shall be made to dispose of such appeal within six months from the date on which the appeal is presented to the High Court.

Explanation- For the purposes of this section, 'High Court' means the High Court within the jurisdiction of which the .
land acquired or proposed to be acquired is situated.

5. As per Section 74 of the Act, the appeal shall be filed within 60 days, from the date of award, and as per proviso added to Section 74 of the Act, High Court, if satisfied, can condone the delay of 60 The Secretary vs Manjeet Singh on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41269092/
2 days.
The legislature in its wisdom, has prescribed period of 60 days, which can be condoned, if the applicant is able to make out a case for condonation of delay.
In such situation, general provision of Section 5 of the Limitation Act, is not applicable, in view of the bar, as created by Section 74 of the Act.
Thus, the delay which is more than 60 days, cannot be condoned, by this Court.
6. Consequently, the application for condonation of delay is dismissed.
(Virender Singh) Judge 10.05.2024 Kalpana .
